stem: A Restoril prescription issued on January 10 is presented for another refill on July 11; one authorized refill remains. What should the pharmacist do?

choices.text: Dispense because one authorized refill remains on the profile.
Measure six months from the most recent refill date.
Decline the refill because the prescription is now more than six months past its issue date.
Transfer the record and let the receiving pharmacy restart the clock.
Use the Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity rule.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Decline the refill because the prescription is now more than six months past its issue date.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Dispense because one authorized refill remains on the profile.' would require that unused authorization survived after the prescription became more than six months old. The decisive cue appears in 'A Restoril prescription issued on January 10 is presented for another refill on July 11; one authorized refill remains. What should the pharmacist do?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Dispense because one authorized refill remains on the profile.' would apply only if unused authorization survived after the prescription became more than six months old; 'A Restoril prescription issued on January 10 is presented for another refill on July 11; one authorized refill remains. What should the pharmacist do?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Measure six months from the most recent refill date.' would apply only if 21 CFR 1306.22 measured from last dispensing rather than issue; 'A Restoril prescription issued on January 10 is presented for another refill on July 11; one authorized refill remains. What should the pharmacist do?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Decline the refill because the prescription is now more than six months past its issue date.': supported by schedule iii-iv refills.
choice_analysis.D: 'Transfer the record and let the receiving pharmacy restart the clock.' would apply only if transfer created a new issue date; 'A Restoril prescription issued on January 10 is presented for another refill on July 11; one authorized refill remains. What should the pharmacist do?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Use the Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity rule.' would apply only if temazepam were Schedule II rather than Schedule IV; 'A Restoril prescription issued on January 10 is presented for another refill on July 11; one authorized refill remains. What should the pharmacist do?' states otherwise.

related_facts: temazepam (Restoril) is used for short-term treatment of insomnia; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
